steps.title: What is an XY plot?
steps.markdown:
An **XY Plot** traces one signal against another in real time — X on the horizontal axis, Y on the vertical axis.

Unlike a time plot, there is no shared time axis. The trace shows the *relationship* between two quantities directly.

In this tutorial you will drive both axes with **Signal Generator** datasources to produce a Lissajous-like closed curve.

steps.title: Create a pane
steps.markdown: Click **Add pane** in the header to create your workspace area.

steps.title: Create the X-axis datasource
steps.markdown:
Open **Datasources**, click **ADD**, choose **Signal Generator**.

Give it the name **Signal X** and set **Refresh Every (ms)** to **100**. Leave the waveform as **Sine**. Click **ADD**.

steps.title: Create the Y-axis datasource
steps.markdown:
Add a **second** Signal Generator.

Name it **Signal Y**, set **Refresh Every (ms)** to **100**, and change the **Phase** to **90** degrees so the two signals are offset — this produces a circular trace. Click **ADD**.

steps.title: Add the XY Plot widget
steps.markdown:
On your pane, click **Add widget**. In the widget picker, choose **XY Plot Widget** and click **OK**.

The XY plot editor will open next so you can bind the sources.

steps.title: Bind X and Y sources
steps.markdown:
In the **XY Plot editor**:

1. Under **X Source**, set **Datasource** to **Signal X**.
2. Under **Y Source**, set **Datasource** to **Signal Y**.
3. Click **Save**.

The step completes once both sources are bound to Signal Generator datasources.

steps.title: Tutorial complete
steps.markdown:
Your XY plot is live.

- **Signal X** drives the horizontal axis.
- **Signal Y** (90° offset) drives the vertical axis.
- The closed circular trace is a simple Lissajous figure.

Try changing the waveforms, frequencies, or phase in the Datasources panel to explore different trace shapes.
